assumptions: Analytical sites can implement harmonized SOPs and capture-compatibility panels.
A characterized exogenous intact-EV spike-in tracer is available and distinguishable from endogenous material at all sites.
Pilot lots can be produced with sufficient yield to split and ship blinded aliquots under controlled cold-chain.
biological_rationale: MISEV2023 and program rodent evidence indicate that orthogonal, membrane-protection–based identity and protected-cargo signals are necessary to attribute activity to intact EVs and to avoid false confidence from bulk particle metrics alone (ev-misev2023-quality-framework; ev-hermann-2023-neonatal-hi). A blinded, multi-site reproducibility demonstration with spike-in controls directly addresses the identified lot-comparability gap and reduces the risk that an apparent fingerprint is an assay artifact or site-specific phenomenon (ev-driedonks-2022-macaque-biodistribution highlights the translational risk of assuming particle counts predict exposure).

candidate_quality_attributes.measurement_concept: Binary qualitative fingerprint presence/absence determined by harmonized orthogonal assays with spike-in validation.
candidate_quality_attributes.name: Lot-comparability fingerprint (qualitative pass/fail)
candidate_quality_attributes.rationale: A qualitative composite fingerprint avoids premature numeric release limits while enabling go/no-go comparability decisions; it integrates orthogonal identity and protected-cargo signals and is validated by spike-in recovery.

edges.competing_explanation: Apparent conservation of fingerprint across lots could reflect consistent co-isolation of non-vesicular components or site-specific assay harmonization rather than true EV-associated lot consistency.
edges.missing_experiment: A blinded, multi-lot, multi-site study using spike-in controls and harmonized SOPs with a predefined qualitative scoring rubric.
edges.uncertainty: Moderate: guidance and rodent data support the need for orthogonal linkage but do not prove multi-site reproducibility.

edges.competing_explanation: Even if reproducibility is shown, the fingerprint may not predict in vivo delivery in larger species; false confidence could still drive wasted bridging studies.
edges.missing_experiment: Subsequent short-interval in vivo recoverability/bridging studies using lots that pass/fail the fingerprint gate.
edges.uncertainty: Moderate-to-high: cross-species delivery uncertainty increases the programmatic need for a reproducible identity/comparability gate before expensive bridging studies.

nodes.statement: A composite orthogonal fingerprint (capture-positive surface phenotype co-localized with particle peaks; protected-cargo panel; particle:protein context) reflects presence of intact, membrane-protected EV-associated material and can be measured qualitatively.

If the fingerprint is reproducibly observed across independent pilot lots and at multiple analytical sites under blinded conditions with spike-in recovery controls, then it can serve as a non-numeric lot-comparability gate for advancing lots into bridging and potency-linkage studies.

If the fingerprint is not reproducible (discordant blinded calls) despite validated spike-in recovery and capture-compatibility controls, then lot-level variability or assay fragility prevents use of this composite fingerprint for comparability and the program must pursue alternative strategies (tighter fractionation, source-cell specification, or secretome-centric definitions).

competing_explanations: Concordant fingerprint calls could be driven by spike-in or procedural artifacts rather than endogenous EV-associated signals; spike-in controls and buffer-compatibility checks are therefore essential.
Site-to-site concordance could mask upstream lot variability if shipments degrade material; cold-chain and split-aliquot controls are required.
dependencies: Produce >=3 pilot GMP-like lots (representative upstream process and source-cell bank)
Select and qualify two analytical sites; finalize harmonized SOPs and data rubric
Obtain or prepare an orthogonal exogenous intact-EV spike-in tracer with traceable identifier
design_question: Can a predefined, minimal composite orthogonal fingerprint (capture-positive surface-phenotype co-localized with particle peaks + protected-cargo panel + particle:protein context), measured under a harmonized SOP and controlled by an exogenous intact-EV spike-in, be detected reproducibly (binary pass/fail per lot) across pilot lots and independent analytical sites so it can serve as a non-numeric lot-comparability gate without becoming a premature numeric release specification?
expected_measurable_effect: Concordant qualitative fingerprint (pass/fail) calls for the same pilot lot across independent analytical sites, with validated spike-in recovery and capture-compatibility controls; decision rule enabling advancement of passing lots into bridging studies.

experiment.assay: Blinded orthogonal workflow at each site: (1) fractionate aliquot to identify particle-peak fractions; (2) intact immuno-capture ELISA/bead-capture for canonical surface markers on fractions; (3) detergent+protease/RNase protection test on captured material; (4) protected-cargo targeted assays (small-RNA panel + targeted proteomics) on capture-positive fractions; (5) total protein assay and particle:protein context calculation; sites report a binary fingerprint-present/fingerprint-absent call with raw data.
experiment.comparator: Blinded inter-site comparisons per lot: qualitative fingerprint-present versus fingerprint-absent calls across sites; positive control: characterized small-EV reference material blinded and included at each site; negative control: detergent-disrupted aliquots and buffer-only controls.
experiment.control: Per-site spike-in recovery readout per fraction (must be recovered and detergent/protease-sensitive), blinded positive and negative controls, and capture-compatibility buffer-only checks.
dependencies: Production and aliquoting of >=3 pilot GMP-like lots with sufficient yield and cold-chain control
Two or more analytical laboratories with the orthogonal assay capabilities and trained personnel
Availability of characterized exogenous intact-EV spike-in tracer and harmonized SOPs
experiment.failure_criterion: Discordant fingerprint calls across sites for the same lot despite validated spike-in recovery and capture-compatibility checks, or controls reveal signals are due to assay interference or spike-in artifacts.
experiment.falsification_outcome: If falsified, do not use this composite fingerprint for lot comparability; pursue alternative strategies (tighten fractionation, protected-cargo panel redesign, source-cell controls, or secretome-centric definitions) and perform assay harmonization before reattempting.
experiment.hypothesis_tested: A composite orthogonal fingerprint (capture-positive, detergent/protease-sensitive surface phenotype co-localized with particle peaks; protected-cargo panel; particle:protein context) will be reproducibly detectable (same qualitative pass/fail call per lot) across >=3 pilot lots and >=2 analytical sites under blinded conditions when assays include per-sample exogenous intact-EV spike-in recovery and capture-compatibility checks.
experiment.primary_readout: Concordant qualitative fingerprint call per lot across analytical sites (fingerprint reproducible = same qualitative call for a given lot across all participating sites) with validated spike-in recovery and capture-compatibility checks.
experiment.question: Can a harmonized, spike-in-controlled, blinded multi-site assay workflow reproducibly call a minimal composite fingerprint (present/absent) on split aliquots from >=3 pilot lots so the fingerprint can be used as a non-numeric lot-comparability gate?
required_material: >=3 pilot GMP-like production lots aliquoted into split, blinded aliquots (cold-chain tracked)

Harmonized SOP package for fractionation (SEC or iodixanol cushion), particle counting (NTA/TRPS), intact immuno-capture (anti-CD63/CD9/CD81 and TIM4/AnxA5), detergent+protease protection, and protected-cargo targeted assays
Exogenous characterized intact-EV spike-in tracer (orthogonal species or isotope-labeled) to add to each aliquot prior to shipment and assay
Particle counter instrumentation (NTA or TRPS) and consumables at each site
Capture reagents and capture-compatibility buffer panels at each site
Targeted small-RNA panel reagents and targeted proteomics reagents with spike-in standards
Cold-chain shipping materials and chain-of-custody documentation
secondary_readouts: Spike-in recovery and detergent/protease-sensitivity per site and per lot
Protected-cargo panel qualitative presence/absence concordance across sites
experiment.success_criterion: Qualitative success: In blinded testing of >=3 pilot lots across >=2 analytical sites, each lot yields the same qualitative fingerprint call at all sites (concordant pass or concordant fail) and spike-in recovery & capture-compatibility controls confirm assay performance. Achieving concordant 'fingerprint reproducible' calls for >=2 lots (preferably all >=3) permits adopting the fingerprint as a qualitative comparability gate.

explicit_inferences: Inference: orthogonal, membrane-protection–based signals are required to avoid conflating non-vesicular co-isolates with EV identity (MISEV guidance).
Inference: multi-site blinded reproducibility is a prerequisite to adopt a non-numeric comparability gate without premature numeric release criteria.
falsification_criteria: Discordant qualitative fingerprint calls across analytical sites for the same blinded lot despite validated spike-in recovery and capture-compatibility controls (i.e., lack of inter-site concordance).
Spike-in recovery inconsistent across replicates or sites, preventing assay-controlled interpretation.
human_decisions_required: Approve pilot-lot production plan and cold-chain aliquoting scheme
Select participating analytical sites and finalize harmonized SOP/qualitative rubric
Approve the protected-cargo panel and multi-epitope capture panel to be used in the study
manufacturability_assessment: This experiment requires production of >=3 pilot GMP-like lots with split aliquots, harmonized assay SOPs, and logistics for blinded shipments; these are resource-intensive but feasible and directly inform comparability strategy.
manufacturing_rationale: Establishing a reproducible, qualitative fingerprint across pilot lots and sites enables a defensible non-numeric comparability gate for advancing production lots to bridging studies and assay validation, while avoiding premature numeric specifications that may be unstable prior to method robustness and multi-site verification (ev-misev2023-quality-framework).
measurement_strategy: Harmonized SOPs across sites, a binary qualitative scoring rubric (fingerprint present / fingerprint absent) with prespecified rules, per-sample exogenous intact-EV spike-in recovery check, capture-compatibility buffer panels, and centralized data collation for concordance metrics.
novelty_statement: This hypothesis differs from prior program proposals by (A) requiring blinded, split-aliquot multi-site testing under harmonized SOPs and (B) mandating an exogenous intact-EV spike-in as a per-sample assay recovery control and decision-rule gate. Prior hypotheses proposed similar orthogonal fingerprints or multi-site reproducibility in concept, but did not combine blinded split-aliquot ring study design, a prespecified binary qualitative rubric for lot-level pass/fail, and mandatory spike-in recovery checks as the discriminant to prevent assay-driven false concordance.
principal_risks: Spike-in or assay artifacts produce false concordance across sites.
Insufficient lot material or poor cold-chain leads to discordant results unrelated to intrinsic reproducibility.
Even if reproducible, fingerprint may not predict in vivo delivery or clinical translatability.
proposed_potency_relationship: None asserted. The fingerprint is explicitly non-potency (comparability/identity) for now; subsequent studies can test whether fingerprint-positive lots are enriched for potency in mechanism-linked assays.
proposed_product_change_or_attribute: Adopt a non-numeric lot-comparability fingerprint (qualitative pass/fail) composed of: (A) intact-material immuno-capture positive signal for canonical EV surface markers that co-localizes with particle-count peaks and is detergent/protease-sensitive; (B) a small protected-cargo panel (protected miRNA subset + at least one detergent-sensitive luminal protein) detected in capture-positive, particle-peak fractions and lost after membrane disruption; and (C) conserved particle:protein context. The composite fingerprint is to be used as a qualitative comparability gate to advance pilot lots into bridging studies (not as a numeric release test).
title: Blinded multi-site, spike-in–controlled fingerprint reproducibility study to establish a non-numeric lot-comparability gate for SGL-001
